receipts.first_text_witness: A real estate agent handed me a flyer last weekend at an open house. Glossy, folded in thirds, smelled faintly of toner. The headline across the top said, "Your starter home awaits." The photo was a 1,500 square foot split-level with original windows and a kitchen that hadn't been updated since the Clinton administration.
receipts.last_text_witness: The mortgage industry has no reason to bring it up. The real estate industry has no reason to bring it up. So, it falls to people running the numbers at their kitchen table, one at a time, to notice what has happened. Run your own numbers. Be honest about what you see. And if the math doesn't work, that's not you failing the system. That's the system telling you the truth.

primary_source_receipts.finding: Freddie Mac reports a 6.30% average 30-year fixed rate on April 30, 2026. A $675,000 30-year loan at 6.30% amortizes at about $4,178 monthly before taxes and insurance, matching the transcript's rounded $4,177.
The 2022 SCF table reports an $8,000 median transaction-account balance among families holding such accounts, in 2022 dollars. It is not a current 2026 savings-account balance for all households.

primary_source_receipts.claim: First-time buyer share, age and family assistance
primary_source_receipts.finding: NAR reports first-time buyers at 21%, median age 40, and gifts or loans from family and friends used by 22%. The survey covers successful primary-residence buyers and had a 3.5% adjusted response rate.
ACS S1901 estimates 15.6% of U.S. households had income of $200,000 or more in 2024, not 12%-13%. Income alone does not establish ability to afford the modeled home.

primary_source_receipts.claim: Private mortgage insurance cancellation and automatic termination
primary_source_receipts.finding: Borrowers may request cancellation at 80% of original value subject to conditions, while automatic termination generally occurs at scheduled 78% if current. Loan type and payment history matter, so a universal nine-year duration is not supported.

primary_source_receipts.claim: Housing and total debt expense ratio definitions
primary_source_receipts.finding: FHFA distinguishes the front housing-expense ratio from the back total-debt expense ratio. Applying 36% only to housing and calling it affordability mixes concepts; maintenance is also a household budget item rather than a standard mortgage payment field.

primary_source_receipts.claim: Q1 2026 foreclosure starts and bank repossessions
primary_source_receipts.finding: ATTOM reports foreclosure starts up 20% year over year and 14,020 repossessions, up 45%, in Q1 2026. These changes do not identify $750,000 buyers or a particular origination vintage as the cause.
The report states roughly 40% of working Americans report living paycheck to paycheck. It does not support the transcript's claim that 40% specifically among people earning $300,000-$500,000 do so.

NAIC reports the nationwide average HO-3 premium rose 11.26% from 2021 to 2022 and emphasizes state and coverage variation. This does not support the transcript's exact 57% since 2019, 12% in 2025 or $4,500-$5,500 national budget without an identified source and coverage definition.

ICE reports a 3.42% national delinquency rate in September 2025 and separately elevated FHA performance near 11%. The transcript's unlabeled 11.5% national-sounding claim lacks the required loan-class denominator.

calculation_receipts.assumptions: Frozen views and age_days; exact listed same-channel long-form peers under build_baseline.compare; first five listed peers for sensitivity.

calculation_receipts.method: Independent mortgage, budget and investment arithmetic
calculation_receipts.assumptions: Mortgage uses $675,000 principal, 6.30% nominal annual rate, monthly compounding and 360 payments. Investment projections use annual compounding for lump sum and monthly end-of-period contributions; taxes, fees, inflation and volatility omitted only to reproduce claims.
